To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cytochrome c, the protein which is thought to be the initiator of apoptosis, is dispensable for caspase activation after ATP-depletion and that cytochrome-c induced cell death in Jurkat cells, which was not observed in SKW6 cells, is independent of the presence of ATP.
cytochrome c, a mitochondrial protein thought to play a key role in apoptosis, is not required for Fas-induced casapase activation and apoptosis.
cytochrome c does not play a major role in Fas-induced apoptosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
apoptosis, a type of programmed cell death.
the molecular mechanism of Fas-induced apoptosis.
the role of the mitochondrial cytochrome c in the initiation of apoptotic cell death.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of cytochrome C is not essential for Fas-induced cell apoptosis.
cytochrome c plays no role in the initiation or propagation of caspase activation or apoptosis following Fas ligation.
cytochrome c does not seem to play any role in the induction of apoptosis in the cell systems used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mitochondrial pathway of apoptosis is dispensable for Fas-induced cell-death.
the release of cytochrome from mitochondria is not necessary for Fas-induced casapse activation and apoptosis.
cytochrome c plays an important role in caspase-activation and apoptosis only if the cell is not ATP-depleted.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cytochrome c does not seem to be a necessary component of the Fas pathway, and that the mitochondrial release of cytochrome may be a consequence of the Fas-induced apoptotic pathway.
ATP-depleted cells are not a suitable model system for investigating the role of cytochrome-c in apoptosis.
the release of cytochrome from the mitochondria is not required for caspase activation.
